Special: You cannot reduce this power's damage to you by any means. Other creatures' resistances and immunities work normally.

presentation.description:
Effect: Ask three questions. For each, make an *Arcana, Diplomacy, or Insight check*. Use the target's level and an *Easy, Normal, or Hard DC*, depending on its attitude toward you at death and how protective it is of the information. On a success it gives a short answer, usually no longer than a minute.

Special: At the GM's discretion, you may contact uneasy spirits that have not moved on, regardless of how long they have been dead. Using this against undead or during combat is possible but very difficult.

presentation.description:
Effect: You may drop, sheathe, or store what you hold, then draw one or two firearms. If wielding two firearms, you can target one additional creature within 5 squares of the first.

Hit: 1[W] damage, and the target cannot take opportunity actions until the end of your next turn. When making two attacks, one target takes the primary-hand weapon's damage and the other the off-hand weapon's damage. *Level 11:* 2[W]. *Level 21:* 3[W].

Special: This power does not provoke opportunity attacks.

presentation.title: Docker

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist leader theme.

sections.text-1: Flint's docks bring together poorly paid laborers, educated engineers, and refugees from the wars between Danor and Drakr. Their shared culture has produced graffiti artists, musicians, dancers, and amateur philosophers who brighten soot-covered warehouses and challenge public figures with humorous moral puzzles. Fey pepper, strong drink, and lively arguments are common companions to their art.
sections.text-2: Sometimes their criticism becomes too pointed or their gatherings turn into riots. Both dockers and police have suffered in these clashes, and accidental deaths strain relations. Governor Roland Stanfield nevertheless has a soft spot for these mild anarchists.
sections.text-3: You need not perform publicly to share the docker spirit: anyone who endures hard work and low wages while appreciating intelligent art belongs. As conditions worsen, workers increasingly look to dockers for relief. A good docker also needs to survive a scrap.
sections.text-4: Some leave the scene with help from sympathetic bar owners or police, spreading docker culture into slums and farms. One popular song tells of a graffiti artist who fled to Crisillyir and now paints subversive interpretations of Clergy doctrine in cathedrals.
sections.text-9: The *Notorious Celebrity* paragon path (guide p. 28) lets reputation itself affect your enemies. Musician and adventurer Rock Rackus claims to have explored fiery dungeons, visited the moon, and cuckolded a fey king.

sharedData.title: Docker

presentation.title: Eschatologist

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist controller theme.

sections.text-1: The Heid Eschatol movement began with the Drakran dwarf Vlendam Heid's treatise _On the Proper Endings of Things_. Its account of the Lost Riders explained the dwarven habit of defining civilizations and eras by their endings. In three decades, it inspired an academic discipline devoted to ending everything properly: romances, friendships, business arrangements, wars, serialized stories, and lives.
sections.text-2: Heid's disciples are eschatologists, students of the world's end. Their popularity reinforces Drakr's fascination with apocalyptic prophecy. The Clergy denies that the dwarven endtimes are near and distrusts the movement.
sections.text-3: Dwarves of many nations sympathize with Heid. Veterans of the border wars often find comfort in an orderly judgment day. Apocalyptic cults are increasingly treated as religious sects rather than fringe madness, although most adherents outside Drakr seek reasoned acceptance of death rather than expect imminent destruction.
sections.text-4: Consider life's thresholds and endings, keep your will updated, and learn your companions' wishes should they die. Some followers rush toward death; most carefully guard against an accidental demise that would spoil their plans.
sections.text-9: The *Logos* paragon path (guide p. 25) allows speech to alter reality. Grandis Komanov leads frost-bitten, beardless dwarves in the far north; rumor says she exists partly at the end of time and no living creature can harm her.

presentation.title: Gunsmith

sharedData.concept: Designers and wielders of custom firearms.

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist striker theme.

sections.text-1: Fusils have existed for centuries, using explosive alchemy to propel bullets. They once compared poorly with accurate, safer magic. After the Great Malice, Danor refined them into modern guns. Industrial production now equips armies in Risur and Drakr with firepower comparable to trained sorcerers.
sections.text-2: Gunsmiths do more than buy weapons: they tinker, trade secrets, and combine chemistry with spellcraft now that guns have spread beyond Danor's dead-magic lands. Governor Stanfield plans an exposition in Flint to display such inventions.
sections.text-3: You might practice trick shots endlessly, enchant your pistols, admire their appearance, or use the fear they inspire. Some decorate their weapons with elaborate inlays and romanticize their deadly purity. Others see only cheap, efficient killing. Lerema Kurtz supposedly conjures a cannon from her petticoat pocket.
sections.text-9: The *Mad Shootist* paragon path (guide p. 26) explores freeze rays, rocket launchers, and shrink rays. Trekhom's arms markets offer conventional explosives and ballistics; its harbor cannons can crack ironclads. Flint's autumn Kaybeau Arms Fair attracts inventors from many nations.

sharedData.title: Gunsmith

presentation.title: Martial Scientist

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist striker theme.

sections.text-1: Danoran war academies teach combat as a science. Students write theses on famous warriors and defend theorems about swordplay alongside their physical training. Danor honors graduates as other nations honor poets and sculptors, and successful techniques have inspired similar schools throughout Lanjyr.
sections.text-11: This theme rewards collecting unusual techniques and exploiting niche situations. The *Polyhistor* paragon path (guide p. 29) lets you devise techniques in battle. Henri Jierre, founder of the Jierre Sciens d'Arms academy, supposedly needed no more than three sword strokes to defeat any foe.
sections.text-2: Students study anatomy through autopsies, the physical principles of attack and defense, and the psychology and sociology of war—from an invasion's human cost to a particular sword technique's cultural meaning.
sections.text-3: Risur's Banhaman Academy in Slate produces siege engineers and artillerists; the Battalion outside Flint trains outstanding wilderness forces. Even small schools run by retired soldiers produce contentious theses, such as one contrasting a single stealthy rapier with twin long swords.
sections.text-4: Drakran schools stress endurance and fighting with scarce resources. Crisillyiri schools emphasize theology and monstrous anatomy. Ber's war college maintains a vast collection of battle songs, supposedly to improve courage and accuracy, perhaps simply to calm its students. Work with the GM to decide your thesis, unless you left before graduating.

sharedData.title: Martial Scientist

presentation.title: Skyseer

sharedData.concept: Folk prophets who read the stars.

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist leader theme.

sections.text-1: Ancient lore speaks of mortals traveling to the stars with lost magic. Druids first noticed connections between celestial motions and worldly affairs, discovered paths into the Dreaming and Bleak Gate, and helped King Kelland defeat the fey titans. For over a millennium, skyseers watched the heavens and awaited prophetic dreams that guided heroes and averted disasters. At Srasama's fall, their warnings saved hundreds of eladrin women.
sections.text-2: Their visions have grown vague in recent centuries. They failed to foresee Danor's industrial rise or prevent many tragedies. Risur still observes their rituals, but their influence is fading and few young people join them.
sections.text-3: Perhaps childhood stargazing led to a prophetic dream and apprenticeship to an elder druid. You learned the planets, stars, and their influences. Precise visions are rare, yet travel magic still works best under a full moon, and sailing when Jiese turns retrograde in the Mad Pirate constellation foretells disaster.
sections.text-4: Skyseers favor night and can tell time as accurately as a clock by glancing at the stars. Many Risuri captains refuse to sail beyond sight of land without one. Old ties provide welcome in many homes and villages, provided you avoid unwelcome prophecy. Read the guide's *Planets and Planes* sidebar (p. 48).
sections.text-9: The *Applied Astronomist* paragon path (guide p. 23) manifests the planets' powers. You may discover why skyseer visions have become so vague.

sharedData.title: Skyseer

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist controller theme.

sections.text-1: Industrial weapons put lethal power within ordinary people's reach. Spirit mediums ask why knowledge of the soul should remain the preserve of priests. Some exploit grieving aristocrats, but others use psionic meditation—a séance—to contact the dead.
sections.text-2: A few reserve this talent for those in sincere need and train only like-minded students. Most reject such exclusivity as another form of organized religion and gladly awaken a spirit for a few coins.
sections.text-3: The Royal Homeland Constabulary eagerly recruits people who can question the recently dead. Investigations involve fewer family messages than ordinary medium work, although conveying such messages can persuade an otherwise uncooperative spirit to reveal secrets.
sections.text-8: The *Urban Empath* paragon path (guide p. 32) communicates with the spirits of cities and invokes their powers. The famous halfling medium Jared Smithee fled after claiming to receive a message from Danor's last Sovereign at the state funeral.

sharedData.title: Spirit Medium

presentation.title: Technologist

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist controller theme.

sections.text-1: Technologists tinker, invent, collect, study, and pester engineers. Their devices often sit on the border between clever and impractical. Danoran academies teach specialized fields; Drakran masters oversee large teams of apprentices. Crisillyir and its Elfaivaran colonies punish such work with holy flagellation, while native eladrin find technology as unsettling as the inhabitants of the Dreaming do. Ber's court, by contrast, welcomes enterprising inventors.
sections.text-10: The *Steamsuit Pilot* paragon path (guide p. 30) builds a machine you can wear in battle. Risuri industrialist Benedict Pemberton, wealthy from ordinary factories, is reportedly recruiting engineers and mages for a secret project involving more exotic creations.
sections.text-2: Law enforcement and militaries struggle to keep pace after centuries of swords, armor, bows, and magic. They enlist specialists to explain strange devices and build custom tools. Mass production supplies common equipment, but custom inventions remain rare.
sections.text-3: Carry disposable tools and weapons for unexpected problems. You might study magic or alchemy too; every technologist has a different vision of what invention can accomplish.

sharedData.title: Technologist

presentation.title: Vekeshi Mystic

sharedData.concept: Patient protectors who rebuild after tragedy.

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist defender theme.

sections.text-1: When Srasama died and nearly all eladrin women perished, many survivors sought suicidal vengeance. The composer Vekesh taught that defeat becomes a final tragedy only if survivors let the story end there. Revenge distracts from grief without creating value; resilience, renewal, and prosperity truly thwart an enemy's goals.
sections.text-10: The *Vekeshi Excoriant* paragon path (guide p. 33) channels Srasama's power. Keep the order's secrets from other players and ask the GM about mystics operating in Flint and beyond.
sections.text-2: His teachings saved isolated eladrin communities and spread throughout Lanjyr as guidance for coping with loss. Most followers avoid violence. The public nevertheless associates “vekeshi” with terrorists and murderers, because the order's rare battle-trained mystics take up arms to protect vulnerable people.
sections.text-3: Casual study is open to anyone; mystical initiation is painful and secret. Taken into the Dreaming, initiates relive Srasama's fall through psychic illusions. Imprisonment, poisoned food, and starvation teach endurance and patience. Burning and magical healing seal the flames' power into them. Recovery in luxury follows, alongside instruction in philosophy and discretion.
sections.text-4: Mystics return to ordinary lives and seek influence in armies, law enforcement, or the underworld to punish those who repeatedly threaten people rebuilding their lives. Secret festivals take place in the Dreaming on irregular lunar holidays. Only rarely does a mystic act openly, wearing eladrin armor and a concealing mask as Srasama's hand against a perpetrator of great suffering.

sharedData.title: Vekeshi Mystic

presentation.title: Yerasol Veteran

limitations: Shared authoring data; runtime theme mechanics are not implemented.

sharedData.description: Zeitgeist defender theme.

sections.text-1: The lush Yerasol Archipelago hosted two centuries of intermittent war between Risur and Danor over wealthy plantations. Thousands died amid its rainforests and flowered beaches. Survivors escaped infections, injury, and trauma to turn military glory into wealth or political influence.
sections.text-2: Poets celebrated the greatest deeds of four wars, the last ending seven years ago. Some supposed heroes merely survived to take credit for another's courage; others performed extraordinary acts and lived to have witnesses tell their stories.
sections.text-3: Everyone recognizes a few veterans' names. Your story made you something of a celebrity, even if you dislike retelling it. Public admiration does not erase memories of dead friends.
sections.text-4: Risur and Danor have learned to support their heroes with comfortable jobs and help returning to civilian life. Neither wants a decorated veteran becoming a public embarrassment. This aid lets many become community pillars, but quickly disappears if a hero criticizes the homeland.
sections.text-9: The *Monument of War* paragon path (guide p. 27) brings wartime memories to life as gunfire and artillery. The source also recommends the naval rules in _Seas of Zeitgeist_, Appendix K (p. 516), or E.N. Publishing's _Admiral o' the High Seas_. King Aodhan famously sailed into Danor's capital harbor, seized its flagship, and sailed home with the prize.

sharedData.title: Yerasol Veteran
